summary: No local short-term rental law. Nothing appears in the town's current local-law index, which I checked directly.
caveat: Separately, and from secondary sources rather than the index: a 2020 draft was reportedly pulled after a petition said to carry around 1,400 signatures.

summary: Local Law #2 of 2023. Annual permit plus inspection. No cap and no owner-occupancy requirement. Occupancy runs two per bedroom plus two; more than eleven guests triggers site plan review. The permit does not transfer on sale.
Chapter 133. Annual permit expiring 31 December plus annual inspection. No cap, no owner-occupancy. Host must be reachable by phone and within 30 minutes by car. Fines up to $5,000.

Chapter 194, Local Law 2 of 2022. In my read, the most workable law in Ulster County right now. Annual permit plus fire and safety inspection. No cap currently enacted, though the board may set one by annual resolution. No owner-occupancy requirement. Single-family and permitted accessory apartments only , so no two-family or multifamily. One parking space per bedroom.

Annual license per unit. No cap, no owner-occupancy. Two per bedroom plus two, to a maximum of ten without Department of Health involvement. One space per bedroom and a 24-hour local contact. Covers Callicoon Center and Hortonville.
Registration certificate from the code enforcement officer plus an annual fee. Out-of-county owners must name a local manager.
Certification and inspection, with no limit on the number of short-term rentals.

No short-term rental law. I read the full Town Code and the Zoning Law, both last amended 30 September 2024, and searched them for short-term rental, transient occupancy, vacation rental and rental registration. Nothing. The only lodging category in the code is a bed-and-breakfast, defined as owner-occupied with no more than five guest bedrooms. This is the most useful unregulated town near Kingston: real inventory, Kingston-area demand, and the city's cap does not reach it. Two honest caveats. The zoning law incorporates its use table by reference and keeps it at the Town Clerk's office, so I have not read how transient lodging is classified district by district. And the town's local-laws web page renders empty, so I cannot rule out something adopted since September 2024.

No dedicated short-term rental law. Chapter 110, adopted by Local Law 4 of 2021, is a general rental registration chapter. It defines "short-term rental" and "non-owner-occupied short-term rental," then does nothing with them: there is no STR permit, no cap, and no prohibition on non-owner-occupied short-term rentals anywhere in it. What you need is a residential rental registration permit, valid one year, with a property maintenance inspection. This is the single most-confused pair on this page. The Ulster County Comptroller's own report says the Village of New Paltz and the Town of Hurley ban all non-owner-occupied short-term rentals. It says the Village . Plenty of summaries have read that as the Town and repeated it. The Town and the Village of New Paltz are different governments with different rules, and a New Paltz mailing address does not tell you which one you are in. Check the parcel, not the envelope. My caveat: I read Chapter 110 in full and the article list of the zoning chapter, but not every section of zoning. I am confident there is no ban; I would not call it airtight.
No short-term rental law of its own as of mid-2026. Very little inventory.

No short-term rental law found for the village itself. Red Hook is three separate governments and only the Town and the Village of Tivoli have their own rules, so the restrictive Town of Red Hook terms below do not reach inside the village boundary. Confirm with the Village Clerk before relying on this: an absence is the hardest thing to prove, and the village has adopted land-use law in other areas.

No short-term rental law and no zoning. I checked the town's local-law index directly and found no rental chapter of any kind, and the town's 2020 Comprehensive Plan says Durham "has no zoning ordinances." The Town Board doubles as the planning board. Renting an existing house needs no town permit that I could find. Building something new is different: the Site Plan Review Law (Local Law 2 of 2005) requires site plan review for any change of use beyond a one- or two-family home, and for commercial additions to one. A 20-unit short-term rental project came before the board for site plan review in 2023. Two caveats. The 2017 Building Law is posted only as a scanned image, so I have not read it. And in August 2023 the board discussed short-term rentals as a revenue source, met "a lot of opposition," and noted it "may need to re-visit" the issue. I read every set of board minutes from January 2025 through July 2026 and none has a short-term rental item. About 40% of the town's homes are second homes.
caveat: From Wikipedia rather than town records: the hamlet called East Windham sits on Durham's southern town line, so an East Windham mailing address may be in the Town of Durham, not the Town of Windham. Check the tax map.

summary: Chapter 147, Local Law 1 of 2017. An annual rental registration certificate from the Town Clerk. No cap and no owner-occupancy requirement. An owner whose principal residence is outside Greene County must name a local contact who lives in the county and is available at all times; there is no distance rule. Occupancy is two per unit plus two per bedroom overnight, with no more than one vehicle per two guests. The chapter has no inspection requirement and does not address transfer on sale. Three violations in 24 months lets the Code Enforcement Officer suspend or revoke the certificate. One quirk: the law defines a short-term rental as a stay of eight consecutive days or less, so stays of nine to 29 nights fall outside it. The fee is set by Town Board resolution. I have not read the zoning chapter's use table.

Local Law 3 of 2025, filed with the Secretary of State on 22 September 2025. Every short-term rental needs a permit from the Code Enforcement Officer, expiring 31 December each year. No cap, no owner-occupancy requirement, no per-owner limit, and no hearing for an ordinary permit. Occupancy is two per bedroom plus two; above eleven guests the Planning Board may require site plan approval. Two contacts are required, one answering within 60 minutes around the clock. The permit is not transferable: a buyer files a new application. Fines run $500 to $5,000, and operating without a permit carries at least $5,000 per occurrence. The fee is set by board resolution, and the posted fee sheet is a scanned image I could not read. Check the tax map: many Tannersville addresses are in the Town of Hunter instead, which has its own law.

Zoning Section 4.15, in force since 2021 and amended in 2024. My source is the village's own permit application rather than the law text, which I could not find online. A permit valid for one calendar year, expiring 31 December: $500 per unit to start and $200 per unit to renew. The application states no cap and no owner-occupancy requirement. A contact must be able to reach the property by car within 20 minutes, and the Code Enforcement Officer inspects at least once every three years. Off-street parking must cover full occupancy, with no lawn or street parking. Unusually, the permit is transferable to a new owner who registers with the village and agrees in writing to comply. Not established: which zoning districts allow short-term rentals. This is a separate government from the Town of Catskill, which has a 30-minute host rule.
caveat: Local reporting in February 2024 said the village was seeking state approval for a 4% occupancy tax.

summary: No short-term rental law. I checked the town's local-law listings and searched its website directly, and found nothing on short-term rentals or lodging, and the town's 2026 moratoriums are on cannabis and battery storage, not rentals. The zoning law (Local Law 2 of 2017) is the thing to understand. It lists bed-and-breakfasts, inns and hotels, mostly by Planning Board special use permit, but says nothing about short-term or vacation rentals, and it states that "any use not listed in the Use Table is prohibited." Whether a whole-house rental counts as an ordinary single-family dwelling is a question for the zoning officer, in writing, before you buy. Worth knowing: a "petition pertaining to local Air B&B rental" reached the Town Board as correspondence on 19 August 2026. Nothing about rentals has appeared on an agenda since.

No short-term rental law. The town's code, current through August 2025, has no rental chapter; its three 2026 local laws cover data centers, a zoning map change and a watershed overlay; and the building fee schedule effective May 2026 has no rental fee of any kind. The same zoning question as Cairo applies: Chapter 201 says "any use not listed in Schedules A and B shall be deemed not permitted," and I have not read the schedules, so confirm with the building inspector that a whole-house rental is treated as a dwelling. The Village of Coxsackie inside the town regulates heavily, so check the tax map.

Chapter 148, Rental Property, with short-term rentals added by Local Law 1 of 2023 on 2 October 2023. Registration with the Village Building Inspector, not a permit. No cap, no owner-occupancy rule and no short-term rental operating standards in the chapter. An owner who doesn't live in Ulster County must name a managing agent who does. On a sale, the owner files a sworn statement naming the new owner within 15 days. Fines run $250 to $500 a day. Not checked: whether the village zoning law limits where rentals can operate. This is a separate government from the Town of Saugerties.
caveat: Local reporting at adoption in 2023 said registration is free.

summary: No short-term rental law that I could find, but the town has no website or online code, so this rests on one report: in June 2023 the town supervisor told the Mountain Eagle the board had no interest in regulating short-term rentals. Confirm with the town clerk at 518-299-3186.

No short-term rental law. The town's posted code has no rental chapter, though the town warns its web copy may not be current. The zoning law (Local Law 4 of 2016) lists bed-and-breakfasts, inns and hotels but not short-term or vacation rentals, and states that "any use not listed in the following table is deemed prohibited." The same question as Cairo applies: ask the building department how a whole-house rental is classified before you buy. I have not checked 2026 board agendas.

No short-term rental law. The town's list of local laws on file has no rental or lodging law, and the Land Use Code, updated in 2025, has no short-term or vacation rental use in the text I could read. The same zoning question as Cairo applies: Section 3.1 says "all land uses not included in this table shall be considered prohibited," and the table lists bed-and-breakfasts, boarding houses and country inns but not whole-house rentals. Ask the Code Enforcement Officer (845-586-2074) before you buy. Board minutes from April to August 2026 show nothing on rentals. Very little inventory.

No short-term rental law. The village's local-law page and permit list have nothing on rentals. The zoning law (Local Law 3 of 2013) is the problem. It says a dwelling does not include "hotels, boarding houses or other transient quarters," allows bed-and-breakfasts and hotels only in the business and recreation districts, lists neither in the Village Residential District, and prohibits every unlisted use without a use variance. Whether a whole-house rental in a residential part of the village is legal is unresolved. Ask the Building Inspector in writing before you buy; Village Hall is 518-263-4020. I have not checked village board minutes.

Local Law 3 of 2021. Two-year permit, annual inspection. The cap applies to new non-owner-occupied permits only and resets by 1 August each year as a percentage of housing units; owner-occupied is uncapped. Manager must be within 30 miles of Town Hall. Permitted only in AR-3, AB-3, R-1, R-2, R-5, H and B districts.

Local Law 5 of 2024, §75-28.4. Two-year permit. No town-wide cap, but each owner gets one owner-occupied plus one non-owner-occupied permit . $1M landlord liability required. Local manager with 30-minute response if the owner lives more than 10 miles from Town Hall. Does not transfer on sale. Full detail below.

Local Law 4 of 2019, plus Local Law 1 of 2025. Annual registration through the Building Department, good for one calendar year, with a yearly fire and safety inspection attached to every renewal. One owner-occupied and one non-owner-occupied per owner. Registrations are not transferable. Fees on the town's own application run $100 owner-occupied and $250 non-owner-occupied. Single-family homes and habitable accessory structures only; no tents, trailers or RVs, and no three-or-more-unit buildings unless owner-occupied. The 2025 change is the one that catches people. Local Law 1 of 2025, adopted 18 March 2025, requires any lot with an accessory dwelling unit to be owner-occupied, and prohibits short-term rental of either the main house or the ADU except under a permit issued before Local Law 4 of 2019. That grandfathering dies after six months of inactivity. If the property you are looking at has an ADU, assume short-term rental is off the table unless the seller can show a pre-2019 permit in continuous use. What I could not pin down: the law says the Town Board sets caps on both categories annually by resolution. I could not find the resolution, so I cannot tell you this year's numbers. Ask the Building Department.

Zoning §123-12H. (The amendment history I could read points to Local Law 2 of 2022; a secondary source cites Local Law 8 of 2021. I have not settled which, so take the section number and not the law number.) Annual operating permit from the Building Department, safety inspection required, no cap of any kind in the text. Owner occupancy is not required, but it decides your path: owner-occupied is an inspection and a permit, while non-owner-occupied also needs Planning Board site plan approval , which is a hearing rather than a form. Non-owner-occupied must name a host living within 15 driving miles. Occupancy is two per bedroom plus two. A distinction worth understanding before you write an offer, because it is unusual. The operating permit does not survive a sale: it is "null and void immediately upon a change in ownership." But the site plan approval underneath it does. §123-12H(7)(b): "Existing valid non-owner occupied STR site plan approvals shall transfer to the new owner upon issuance of the new operating permit, unless the subject STR is in violation of this chapter." Read those two conditions carefully. The approval transfers on issuance of your new operating permit , not at closing, and not at all if the property is in violation. Handled properly this is a materially better position than most towns on this page, because you inherit the slow part. Confirm the parcel's standing in writing with the Building Department before you rely on it. Not established: the fee amount, which the code leaves to a town board schedule I could not find, and the exact liability insurance figure.

A dedicated law exists. Chapter 314, Short-Term Rentals, created by Introductory Local Law 1 of 2023, with the state environmental review notice published 3 January 2024 and the law and permit application posted by the town in March 2024. A permit is required. The town's stated purpose is to allow short-term rentals while protecting housing affordability and residential privacy.
caveat: I cannot tell you a single operative term of it. The only published copy of Chapter 314 is a scanned image with no readable text, and the permit application link loops. Secondary sources say annual, non-transferable, single-family only. That is plausible and matches every neighbouring town, but I have not read it and I am not going to repeat it as fact. If you are buying here, call Code Enforcement at 845-336-8853 and ask for an emailed copy of Chapter 314. One trap: this is the Town, a small municipality around Lake Katrine and Sawkill. The 1% cap on whole-home permits you will find all over the internet (106 permits in 2023, 112 as of September 2026) belongs to the City of Kingston, a different government. It does not apply here.

summary: Two-year cycle with a cap on non-owner-occupied permits.
Local Law 3 of 2025. Annual safety license, one per lot, cap possible by resolution.
Local Law 2 of 2022. Zoning Board special permit at $50 plus $150 certificate of occupancy and compliance. Local contact within 20 miles. Non-transferable.
Site plan approval plus inspection plus $500 per year.
Annual permit plus inspection plus a local agent.

Zoning §100-42.1, added by Local Law 7 of 2022 and amended by Local Law 2 of 2024. Two steps: a Planning Board special use permit, then a Building Department short-term rental permit. Permits run two years and expire 31 December; renewals are filed 1 October to 1 December and are themselves subject to the cap on a first-come-first-served basis. Annual inspection by the code enforcement officer. Owner occupancy is not required. Two permits per owner maximum , one owner-occupied and one non-owner-occupied, and that limit follows the people behind an entity, not just the entity. Permits may not be assigned, pledged, sold or otherwise transferred. Allowed as an accessory use to single-family and two-family dwellings in the A, R-2, R-1, R-1/2, R-1/4 and CB districts only. The cap is written as a percentage, not a number: 2% of total dwelling units in the town, amendable by the Town Board at any time. I could not find the current permit count, so I cannot tell you whether there is room. That is the first call to make. Do not confuse the Town of Lloyd, which contains the hamlet of Highland in Ulster County, with the Town of Highland in Sullivan County listed above. Different governments, different laws. The pattern worth internalizing: wherever a zoning board has discretion, as in Hillsdale, Highland, Esopus and Lloyd, getting a permit means a hearing rather than a form. Build that time into the contract.

Chapter 199, Local Law 3 of 2020, amended by Local Law 3 of 2024. An annual permit from the Code Enforcement Officer, renewed by 31 January, with an annual fire inspection added in 2024. No numerical cap. The condition is owner occupancy: a property not occupied by the owner and used mainly for income is a "short-term rental investment property" under the law and needs a special use permit from the Planning Board, which is a hearing, not a form. Every rental needs a local contact living within 20 miles. Occupancy is two plus two per bedroom overnight. Permits are nontransferable and expire on any change of ownership. Three violations in 24 months can mean revocation and up to three years' ineligibility.

Chapter 111, rewritten in full by Local Law 4 of 2023 on 14 August 2023. An annual rental registration certificate from the Village Clerk, at $250 per building plus $100 per unit, with an annual Code Enforcement inspection. The condition is location: new short-term rentals are registered only in the Community Commercial district, capped at 15, and the Village Center district, capped at 10 buildings. Rentals that already existed could register as nonconforming uses, but that status is lost on non-renewal, a transfer without the permit, or six months of disuse. A new owner must file a new registry form within 60 days of closing. Occupancy is two plus two per bedroom overnight. The village also adopted a hotel and short-term rental occupancy tax in 2025 (Local Law 3 of 2025). Not established: whether either cap is full, and what two local laws heard on 21 September 2026 cover, because the posted minutes are scanned images.

also_covers: Modena; check the tax map in Clintondale
summary: Chapter 86, Local Law 4 of 2025, adopted 15 October 2025. An annual permit plus a yearly fire and safety inspection, and the Ulster County registration number must appear in every listing. The condition is the per-owner limit: one owner-occupied and one non-owner-occupied rental per person. The Town Board can also set caps on both by resolution; I have not found that it has. Allowed in every district except GB-80, and not in buildings of three or more units unless the owner lives in one. A host must live within 10 miles and deal with problems within 24 hours. Maximum 10 guests, two per bedroom, one booking at a time, and off-street parking for one car per bedroom plus one. Permits are not transferable. The town ran an amnesty to 1 June 2026 and said it would issue cease-and-desist orders to rentals with no application by 1 May 2026. Fines up to $500 a day.

No dedicated short-term rental law, but the new zoning law covers them anyway. Chapter 205 (Local Law 2 of 2024, adopted 13 June 2024) defines a tourist home as "a dwelling in which overnight accommodations are provided or offered for transient guests for compensation," which describes a whole-house rental, and says a dwelling does not include a tourist home. A tourist home needs a one-year permit from the Building Inspector, issued only after an inspection, and it is unlawful to list or advertise one without a current permit (licensed real estate agents acting only as agents are exempt). The condition is the use tables: tourist home appears only in the Commercial Mixed-Use district, as a special use, which goes to the Planning Board. The Rural Residential and Conservation tables list boardinghouse and bed-and-breakfast but not tourist home. Ask the Building Inspector in writing how a whole-house rental outside the commercial district is treated before you buy. Violations are offenses under the Penal Law: up to $500 and 15 days for a first offense.

Source here is the City of Kingston's own short-term rental fact sheet and housing page rather than the law text. Whole-home permits (STR-F) are capped at 1% of housing units: 112 as of September 2026, per the fact sheet. The cap was reached on 4 March 2024, and as of 12 October 2026 the city's housing page says it is not accepting new Full registrations. There is a waitlist, and joining it takes proof of ownership. Permits do come back when holders don't renew: four reopened in December 2025, through a one-day registration with a random draw. Full permits are allowed only in the T4 and T5 transects. $650/yr for STR-F, $125 for STR-RO and STR-L. Resident-occupied and limited categories are uncapped. One short-term rental per property, none in ADUs. Correction, 12 October 2026: this entry previously gave the cap as about 106 and said whole-home requests are rejected until further notice. 106 was the figure when registration opened in 2023, and the December 2025 reopening shows permits do return through the waitlist. Full detail: Can you still get a short-term rental permit in Kingston, NY?

Zoning §120-17.1, added by Local Law 4 of 2019, and the most restrictive law on this page. Fifteen permits, village-wide , allocated by public lottery once a year. Property must be the owner's primary residence. Sixteen rental days in any calendar year , with a seven-day gap required between rentals. Annual inspection before the permit issues. Non-hosted single-family, two-family or accessory dwelling units, one to three bedrooms. The code contains no transfer clause, but between an annual lottery and a fifteen-permit ceiling, a buyer should assume nothing carries over. Currency caveat: the published code snapshot ends 14 May 2024 and the village's own application page blocks automated reading, so confirm before relying on it.

The town adopted, and most summaries still say it is working on it. Zoning Chapter 125, Article XV, added 29 September 2025 by Local Law 2 of 2025, following amendments in 2024. There is no cap of any kind. The gate is occupancy instead: the property "must be the owner's primary residence," and during the rental the owner must be on site, in the main house or an accessory structure. Two narrow exceptions: a farm stay on land in a certified New York Agricultural District, and an adjacent property the owner occupies, capped at 1,000 square feet. "The short-term rental permit is not transferable to a new owner." Permits run two years. Two people per bedroom, twelve maximum, ten where septic governs. A special use permit is additionally required in the Rhinecliff districts. Prohibited in condominium apartments and on campgrounds and tent platforms. Update, 14 October 2026: the moratorium passed, without short-term rentals. The town board adopted Local Law 3 of 2026 on 14 September 2026, a temporary moratorium on land use applications for conference centers, country inns, agritourism, hotels, motels and special event venues. The draft that went to hearing on 18 August had listed short-term rentals too. The adopted law takes them out: the board found that bed-and-breakfasts and short-term rentals "should be excluded" because the town already has adequate zoning provisions for them. It runs nine months from filing with the Secretary of State, extendable once by up to six months. So the short-term rental rules above are unchanged. Still live: a proposed occupancy tax. At its 5 October 2026 special meeting the board introduced a local law for a 3% hotel room occupancy tax whose definition of a tourist facility reaches short-term and vacation rentals. Public hearing: 9 November 2026, 6:00 pm. It is a proposal, not law. Town Clerk: (845) 876-3409.
Primary residence, roughly 60 nights a year, owner must reside 50 or more days.

Zoning §210-33, added 13 September 2021 and amended 26 April 2022. Short-term rental is allowed in every zoning district provided the property is owner-occupied . It must be the record owner's principal domicile, and the owner has to be on the premises during the stay. Non-owner-occupied is prohibited outright, which the Ulster County Comptroller independently confirms. Permit runs one calendar year and renews automatically; inspection within 30 days of application and again before each renewal. $250 a year on the town's application. One-family, two-family or an accessory dwelling unit only; not a shed, garage, rec room or RV. The occupancy cap is the thing that breaks the spreadsheet. §210-33(A)(6): "An STR shall host no more than two guests per bedroom and is limited to a maximum capacity of six people per dwelling. Children eight years of age and under are not counted as guests." Six people, whatever the bedroom count. A four or five bedroom Hurley house does not earn a four or five bedroom nightly rate here. And the clause a buyer needs. The permit does not simply transfer. Within 60 days of taking title the new owner must show the Building Department that the property is their principal residence, and if they cannot, the department revokes the permit. You inherit a 60-day clock and a residency test, not an income stream.

Chapter 101, Article I, adopted by Local Law 2 of 2022 and amended in 2024. Licences come from the Town Clerk, run twelve months, and carry a fire and safety inspection before the first one and every third year after. No cap on residents. There is a cap on non-residents, and the town's own page says it has been met and it is not issuing . Fees on the town's application: $150 one-time, then $500 a year for an absent owner on a one-bedroom, $400 resident owner, $300 owner-occupied, plus per-bedroom add-ons. Two guests per bedroom, children under 16 not counted. No exterior advertising. Gatherings over twenty prohibited. One rentable unit per parcel. Two provisions decide deals here. First, a one-year ownership wait: "For a property purchased after the effective date of this article, proof of a one-year ownership of a property is required for an STR." You cannot close and start renting. Second, licences "may not be transferred or assigned upon the lease, sale or conveyance of the real property," and the law closes the obvious workaround by terminating the licence if 50% or more of the holding entity changes hands. Buying the LLC does not buy the licence. A conflict I could not resolve: the codified law sets the non-resident cap at 150. The town's own short-term rental page says 100. The code lets the board adjust by resolution, which would explain it, but I could not find the resolution. The practical answer today is the same either way: closed to non-residents.

Zoning §260-56, with definitions added by Local Law 1 of 2019. Three categories. An STR home (one to two bedrooms, four lodgers) and an STR establishment (three to five bedrooms, ten lodgers) both require the owner to reside on the property. STR non-owner-occupied is allowed, whole house, but requires a designated host living within ten miles and is limited to 180 days a year and no more than 26 weekends . One non-owner-occupied registration per owner, and a corporation whose owners hold interests in more than one is prohibited outright. Fees were reset by the Town Board on 3 January 2025 to $250 owner-occupied in-home, $350 owner-occupied separate unit and $450 non-owner-occupied, each plus $25 per additional bedroom.
caveat: On the cap, I do not have a number I trust, and I want to be explicit about why. A cap exists: the town's own 2023 task force document states as an issue that "we are over what we have authorized as the cap," which is not something you write if none is in force. Local reporting describes an original 2019 cap of 340, later reduced to 285. Neither figure is something I have read in the law. The town's posted short-term rental law is a scanned image with no readable text and the online code truncates before the operative section, so I could not reach it. Treat Woodstock as capped, assume it may be full, and confirm the current number and waitlist position with the Building Department before you underwrite anything. The same goes for whether a permit survives a sale: the 2023 document describes the then-current rule as transferable on a new application within 30 days of closing and recommends ending that, and I cannot tell you which is in force today. The fee figures above come from local reporting of the 3 January 2025 board meeting, not from a town fee schedule. A warning specific to researching this town. Much of what search engines return for "Woodstock short-term rental" is Woodstock, Vermont . The 55-plus-55 permit cap, the $750 and $3,000 fees and the flat "does not transfer with the land" line all come from the Vermont town's FAQ, and they circulate as though they were Ulster County's. Check the letterhead and which state's law a document cites before you believe any number about this town, including from me.

summary: Chapter 114, adopted by Local Law 2 of 2022 and substantially amended 10 June 2025 by Local Law 2 of 2025. Owner-occupied is uncapped. Non-owner-occupied is capped, and the number is set fresh each January at the town board's organizational meeting: the 2026 figure is 24 , set by motion at the 2 January 2026 meeting and recorded in the minutes. Permits expire 1 January, renewals are taken 1 November to 30 December, and inspection plus an annual water test are required every year, not just at the start. Non-owner-occupied is limited to 180 rental days a year . Two guests per bedroom, children 12 and under not counted. Host must live within 30 miles and respond in person within an hour. 2025 fees: $400 non-owner-occupied plus $100 per additional bedroom, $200 owner-occupied, $150 inspection. Operating without a permit is $500 a day. Ownership rules here are tighter than anywhere else on this page. One short-term rental per owner, full stop, and no interest greater than one unit whether held personally or through an entity. Corporations cannot hold a permit at all; only individuals, sole proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs and LLCs. Rental arbitrage is expressly prohibited. Accessory dwelling units are excluded, and three-or-more-unit buildings need a board exception. Permits "may not be assigned, pledged, sold, or otherwise transferred." Both grandfathering clauses in the chapter say the same thing twice over: the permit dies when the property changes hands.

Chapter 129, Article IV, added 23 June 2021 by Local Law 1 of 2021. The village does not license short-term rentals so much as prohibit them: it is unlawful to rent a dwelling for less than 30 consecutive nights, and the prohibition lifts only where the short-term rental is "secondary and incidental to the use of the property as a primary residence." A non-owner-occupied whole-house rental is not permitted in the residential zones. Compliance runs through the annual rental property registration, with an annual inspection. On sale, a new owner must notify the code enforcement official within 15 days; the registration is annual and owner-specific, so do not assume anything carries. Hotel and bed-and-breakfast operations in the commercial districts run on a special use permit instead. See the Town of New Paltz in Tier 1, a different government with much looser rules.

Zoning §155-32.3, added 12 April 2021 by Local Law 2 of 2021. Short-term rental is a special use , not a use of right, listed only in the R, R-1 and R-Ag-1 districts and requiring Planning Board approval. Each owner must also hold an annual operating permit from the Building Department. Short-term here means 30 days or less, a slightly wider net than the 29-night line most neighbours use. Correction, and then a gap I am not going to paper over. An earlier version of this page stated flatly that the owner must be a Town of Marlborough resident. That traced to a secondary summary, not to the code, so I have pulled it. But I want to be straight about what that does and does not mean: I have not been able to read §155-32.3 in full either. The online code truncates before the body of the section and the town's own site blocks automated reading. So I am not replacing "residency is required" with "residency is not required." I am telling you that Marlborough's cap, owner-occupancy rule, transfer provision, renewal terms and fees are all unverified . Of everything on this page, this is the entry I know least about. What I can stand behind: a real law exists, short-term rental is a special use in three districts, and a Planning Board hearing plus an annual Building Department permit are required. For anything else, call the Building Department, and do not let anyone including me tell you what Marlborough requires without a citation.
The operator must be the owner. Maximum 90 nights a year.

Chapter 112, adopted 22 December 2021 by Local Law 6 of 2021. Annual operating permit from the Zoning Enforcement Officer, expiring 31 December, renewable within the three months before. Requires "certification that the property is the owner's primary residence," proven by STAR exemption or equivalent, with farm stays the only exception. One parcel per owner. Day limits are real: hosted single-bedroom rentals up to 210 days a year, everything else 120. "Annual operating permits ... are specific to the designated owner and property and cannot be transferred to other owners or properties." There is also a lighter "registered STR" track, a once-a-year un-hosted rental of under 30 days with no permit fee. "Red Hook" is three governments, and they do not agree. The town law above does not reach the villages. The Village of Tivoli adopted its own Chapter 180 on 14 August 2024: hosted only, with the primary resident staying on the premises during the rental and a notarized certification to prove it, un-hosted whole-house rentals prohibited village-wide , one permit per owner, one-family dwellings only, 60 days a year outside the business districts, and the same non-transferable clause. The Village of Red Hook appears to have no short-term rental law at all: I read its code and found no STR chapter and no transient rental use, only older bed-and-breakfast, boarding house and tourist home categories. The published snapshot ends 14 April 2025, so treat that as not found rather than proven.

Chapter 180, adopted 14 August 2024. Un-hosted whole-house rental is prohibited village-wide . Hosted rental is capped at 60 days a year outside the business districts. The village sits inside the Town of Red Hook but regulates separately, so a parcel with a Tivoli address is governed by this, not by the town chapter above.
Primary residence only, roughly 100 days a year, two-year permit.
Prohibited in R-1/2, R-1/3 and R-1/4. $500 a year where allowed. 60-minute local contact rule.

Local Law 4 of 2023, amending a 2021 law. My source is the town's own short-term rental page and its "STR Basics" summary; the law PDFs themselves are scanned images. Non-resident permits are capped at 62. As of 14 October 2026 all 62 are issued, none are available, and about five applicants are on the waiting list. Resident permits are uncapped. Permits are non-transferable, so buying from a permit holder does not get you a permit: a non-resident buyer joins the waiting list. A rental may sleep no more than 15; above that it is treated as a lodging facility. The owner or emergency contact must live within 30 miles. Three violations in a calendar year means revocation. I have not read how the law defines a resident.
